newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch foreign minister to urge restraint.
newsitem.headline: Dutch foreign minister to urge restraint.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo will urge all parties in Albania to show maximum restraint and respect human rights during a Friday visit to the tiny Balkan state, diplomats said.
"It is important to start a dialogue between all political forces," one diplomat told reporters following a meeting on Thursday of senior officials from the 15 EU countries.
"He will stress also that the state of emergency must not be used to curb basic rights," he added.
Van Mierlo, whose country currently holds the EU presidency, will deliver a message holding out the prospect of more economic assistance if dialogue can take place in a spirit of reconciliation.

Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, whose country currently holds the EU's presidency, told reporters on Wednesday that Van Mierlo had been in contact with Albanian President Sali Berisha and would fly to Tirana on Friday to deliver a firm EU message.

With the Balkan country in turmoil, EU governments have so far failed to come up with a collective approach to the crisis, evoking uneasy memories of the inaction and failures which accompanied the run-up to the wars in former Yugoslavia.
Albania's 11-party opposition Forum for Democracy has appealed to the United States and Europe to help the former Stalinist country find a political solution to avoid civil war.
Between 1991-95 the EU pumped some $450 million dollars worth of economic assistance into the tiny country of some three million.
That made Albania the largest recipient of aid per head under the EU's PHARE programme for the development of former communist countries in central and eastern Europe.
Diplomats said some EU states wanted Berisha to be pressured into holding new elections under a new constitution and setting up a broad-based government.
At least 20 people have died in the unrest in Albania since the collapse of bogus investment funds.

The EU will urge that greater controls be imposed on other investment funds still operating, but has made it clear that it will not bail out the people who lost their savings in the crash of the pyramid schemes.
